strings properly. I believe I saw something like that before (strings  
like "c:\foo" which are in fact c:foo" and have to be "c:\\foo"). The  
likely candidate is "c:\Windows\User settings" where the \U is  
interpreted by Vista as unicode and should actually be "\\U" (to be  
interpreted as a backslash followed by U). Markus, can you check any  
generated commands that use paths, please? I believe a safer way  
would be to push the strings instead of quoting them ...

Cheers,
Simon
